01-linux-origins-and-open-source: Trace Linux from a 1991 kernel project to the distributions powering phones, desktops and servers — and learn to choose between Debian, Ubuntu and RHEL without guessing.
02-open-source-licensing-and-ict-skills: Cut through GPL, BSD and Creative Commons: know which licences let you ship proprietary code, which force you to publish, and how open-source businesses actually make money.
03-command-line-basics-and-help: Work fluently in the shell: compose commands with pipes and quotes, control variables and PATH, and find any answer with man, info, locate and find.
04-directories-listing-and-file-manipula: Navigate the filesystem hierarchy like a native, master ls flags, and create, move, copy and delete files with confidence — including hidden and permission-sensitive cases.
05-archiving-and-searching-data: Compress and archive with gzip, bzip2, xz and tar, redirect streams exactly where you want them, and slice text with head, tail, grep and friends.
06-scripts-and-os-condensed: Turn repeated commands into real shell scripts with variables, arguments, conditionals and exit codes — then pick a distro based on lifecycle, not fashion.
07-hardware-and-storage-condensed: Read a machine from the board up: CPU, RAM, UEFI, disks, RAID, partitions and the /dev and /sys trees that expose them to Linux.
08-networking-and-security-condensed: Follow a packet from MAC address to DNS lookup: IPv4 and IPv6, CIDR, routing, resolv.conf and the account model that keeps a system safe.
09-users-groups-and-permissions-condense: Create users and groups, decode /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, and control access with chmod, ownership and special bits — including what only root can do.
10-special-directories-and-files-condens: Understand /tmp, /run and sticky bits, count hard links, and tell a symlink from a real file — the small filesystem details that cause big surprises.
